turns.text: /navigator Grill me on how timesheet entry parsing works. Intermediate depth: enough to follow the parsing change properly, not every edge case.

Sounds good. I read `src/parse.js` and `src/duration.js` in the current checkout. At that depth we'll cover three things: how a whole file is processed, how one line is split into fields, and how durations are read. One question at a time.

First, the big picture: when `parseEntries` gets the text of a whole timesheet, what does it give back, and what happens when one of the lines can't be parsed?
It gives back an object with `entries` and `errors`. A bad line doesn't stop the run, it goes into `errors` with its line number and the loop moves on to the next line.

That's right. `parseLine` throws when a line is wrong, and `parseEntries` catches that separately for each line (`src/parse.js:25-29`), recording `{ line: index + 1, message }`, so line numbers start at 1. One detail you didn't mention: blank lines are skipped before parsing (`src/parse.js:24`), so they never show up as errors, but they still count toward the line numbers of later lines.

Next question: what does `parseLine` return for this line?

```
2026-09-20 1h30m sprint planning #ops #meetings
```
date is 2026-09-20, minutes is 90, description is 'sprint planning', and tags is ['#ops', '#meetings'].

Almost all correct. The date, the 90 minutes, and the description are right: words that start with `#` are left out of the description (`src/parse.js:16`). The tags drop the `#`, though: `src/parse.js:15` keeps the `#` words and then applies `word.slice(1)`, so you get `['ops', 'meetings']`.

Last question for this depth: which of these durations does `parseDuration` reject, and why? `45m`, `2h`, `90`, `h`
45m and 2h are fine. 90 gets rejected because there's no unit, and h gets rejected because there's no number in front of it.

Correct on all four. The pattern in `src/duration.js:1` allows an optional `<digits>h` followed by an optional `<digits>m`, so `90` doesn't match at all, and neither does a bare `h`. When `parseDuration` throws, the error travels up through `parseLine` and ends up in `errors` for that line, which ties back to your first answer.

That covers the three areas we agreed on at intermediate depth: file-level error handling, field splitting and tags, and durations. Do you want to go deeper, or stop here?
